name: NY-15
label: Safe D

key_factors: Torres holds a Bronx seat that leans Democratic by 27 points and has won easily in every cycle
Torres has raised $7.1M with $13.9M on hand plus $3.8M in outside support, while Republican Stylo Sapaskis shows no reported fundraising
Polymarket prices Torres's reelection at roughly 98 percent
Independent Jose Vega has raised about $333K, the only opposition with any visible resources
model.rationale: Torres combines a 27-point partisan lean, full incumbency, and an overwhelming financial edge against a challenger with no visible campaign infrastructure, and prediction markets price his reelection near certainty. No public polling exists, but the structural fundamentals leave almost no plausible path for an upset.
model.watch: A late surge by independent Jose Vega, who has raised modest sums on an anti-Torres message, or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though the district's composition makes any real threat unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ritchie Torres seeks another term in one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in the country, a Bronx-based seat that favored the party by 27 points in recent fundamentals. He enters the general election with a dominant financial position, having raised over $7 million and holding nearly $14 million in cash, supplemented by outside spending on his behalf with none opposing him.

His Republican opponent, Stylo Sapaskis, has no reported fundraising or campaign resources, and the only opposition with measurable support is independent Jose Vega, who has raised about $333,000. Prediction markets give Torres roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. With no public polling in the race, the outlook rests on the district's heavy partisan tilt and the lopsided resources, both of which point to a comfortable Torres victory.
